# New York Lease Rent Increase Prep

A 9% increase before a lease end date can raise a contract-clarity question, but the safest next step is to gather the paperwork and ask for a written explanation. This is a preparation and communication checklist, not a legal conclusion.

## Questions to Ask and Documents to Gather

| Category | What to ask or collect | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Lease terms | Can you point to the exact clause allowing a rent change on 2026-09-01? | Confirms whether the notice matches the written lease language |
| Renewal timing | Is this increase meant to apply only at renewal, or as a mid-term amendment? | Distinguishes a renewal offer from an in-term change |
| Notice details | When was the notice sent, and what effective date does it list? | Checks timing and whether the notice is clear |
| Rent history | Can you provide the current rent ledger and any prior increase notices? | Helps verify consistency and past practice |
| Lease documents | Signed lease, addenda, renewal offers, amendments, notices, emails, and text messages | Creates a complete record in one place |
| Property details | Is the apartment rent-stabilized, rent-controlled, or market-rate? | Affects how rent changes are usually handled |
| Payment record | Copies of rent payments and proof of delivery for communications | Useful if there is a later dispute about notice or acceptance |
| Management contact | Who is the authorized person for lease changes in writing? | Prevents confusion from informal messages |

### Practical checklist
- Read the lease clause on rent changes and renewal terms word-for-word.
- Save the increase notice exactly as received, including date and sender.
- Gather the signed lease, all addenda, and any renewal paperwork.
- Pull together emails, portal messages, and texts about the increase.
- Ask whether the landlord is proposing a renewal, amendment, or correction.
- Request the calculation behind the 9% increase and the proposed start date.
- Keep paying the current rent on time unless you receive written instructions otherwise.
- Keep all communication calm, brief, and in writing.

## Calm Clarification Email Draft

Subject: Request for clarification on proposed rent increase

Hello [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I received the notice stating that the rent will increase by 9% effective 2026-09-01. I am reviewing the lease and wanted to ask for clarification, since my understanding is that rent changes occur at renewal and the lease term ends on 2026-12-31.

Could you please send:
- The specific lease clause or document supporting the proposed change date
- Whether this is intended as a renewal offer, amendment, or other update
- The current rent ledger and a copy of any related notice or addendum

I want to make sure I understand the request correctly and keep everything documented. Thank you for your help.

Best,
[Your Name]
[Unit Number]
[Phone or Email]

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Save Lease File] https://www.usa.gov/consumer-complaints
Action: [Button: Review NY Housing] https://hcr.ny.gov/rent-stabilization-and-rent-control

- New York State Homes and Community Renewal: https://hcr.ny.gov/rent-stabilization-and-rent-control
- New York State Attorney General, Tenant Rights Guide: https://ag.ny.gov/publications/tenants-rights-guide
- USA.gov consumer help: https://www.usa.gov/consumer-complaints
